full_judgment:
3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint. He contended, inter alia, that the defendant being engaged in the import business of computer accessories opened better of credit being No. IBD/DHAN/99/424 DATED 11.11.1.999 with the plaintiff bank and according to the terms of the bank policy of opening L/C, the defendant deposited some title documents of property and some blank undated but signed cheques, being No. 1238227 and few others against his current account No. 37710 as collateral security for favouring the said L/C/ opened with the bank. As per policy of business, the bank kept some blank delivery order (D/0) and letter pad singed by the importer to enable the bank to fill up and for delivery of goods on receipt of money on behalf of the importer. The defendant opened some other L/C and closed this way one after another but the aforesaid cheques and title documents of property remained with the defendant. The defendant lastly opened Latter of Credit No. IBBL/DHAN/00/103 dated 15.03.2000 for importing computer accessories for an amount of US$ 35,510 mentioning shipment dated 15.04.2000 and expiry date on 10.04.2000 and an amendment of L/C was made on 20.3.2000. The Bank suddenly informed the defendant that bank has received the documents of consignment with some discrepancies and, accordingly, replied the bank of the exporter as per plaintiffs MSG No 352/00 dated 03.02.2000. The defendant could not understand how the consignment came while the Letter of credit had not been performed, even then the plaintiff bank requested the defendant to negotiate the documents requesting for 60% discount on the bill amount. Thereafter, the defendant time and again requested the plaintiff bank to close the matter and return the signed cheques of the defendant and transfer the margin money to his current account, but the plaintiff bank kept on doing the reverse by forcing the defendant to accept the discrepant documents and to make payment to the purported beneficiary. The defendant having no other alternative, served legal notice dated 1st April, 2001 by registered post to return the property documents, cheques and transfer the margin money against the said L/C to his current account within 7 days but the plaintiff did not reply. From the subsequent conduct of the plaintiff bank it was quite. clear to the defendant that the plaintiff deliberately defrauded the defendant and that having failed in all its efforts and endeavours to recover the property documents, transfer of margin money to his current account from the plaintiff, he was compelled to take shelter of the Court of Law for recovery of his property documents, unused cheques and margin money and thereby filed Title Suit No. 127 of 2001 in the Third Court of Sub-Judge, Dhaka, which is pending for disposal, and out of that grudge the instant suit has been filed with ill motive, which is liable to be dismissed. 

 "I. For that the original L/C IBR/DHAN/00/12 dated . 13.01.2000 was for US$ 71,020 and by amendment thereof imported goods to the tune of US$ 35,510 was initially released and thereafter the importer submitted proforma Invoice for the remaining goods under L/C dated 13.01.2000 and for the purpose of release of the goods obtained L/C IBR/DHAN/00/103 dated 15.03.2000 for US$ 35,510, where-upon the goods were released from the Airport and kept in the bank's godown; which the importer got released on obtaining TR facility from the Bank and thereafter got the goods released from the Bank by delivery order (D/0) of 162 pieces of Hard Disk out of 355 pieces Hard Disk and later on refused to release the remaining quantity, the appellate Court decreed the suit on recording such finding of fact but the High Court Division the said finding of fact dismissed the suit on the erroneous view that it was absurd that the goods arrived before the opening of L/C. 

 “I. For that the Courts below having concurrently found that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his case and was not entitled to get back his mortgage deeds and L/C margin deposited with bank till payment of bank dues against the import, the High Court Division erred in holding without any basis that the goods against the L/C No. IBBL/ DHAN/ 00/103 dated 15.03.2000 never arrived into Bangladesh and therefore the plaintiff is entitled to the whole margin amount against the said L/C and any other documents submitted along with it as security for that purpose. 

 II. For that in view of the concurrent finding of fact by the courts below that the plaintiff opened the L/C No. IBBL/DHAN/00/103 dated 15.03.2000 and released the goods pursuant thereto and was thus not entitled to the margin amount and other security documents submitted for the purpose, the High Court Division erred in decreeing the suit on notional view of the case."
